title: The Axis — one continuous three.js instrument holding nine āvaraṇas as weather up the body
what: One continuous three.js instrument, The Axis, holds the nine āvaraṇas as weather stacked up the body (Feet → Totality, 30 units apart) and all 102 Śaktis as points of light standing in their rings. Tapping a light begins the rite of entering, which is itself the travel.
how: Single 3D scene; rings stacked on a vertical axis 30 units apart; each Śakti a point of light; tap → rite → flight → her room; 'rise' carries you up through the nine worlds.
needs: SceneKit/RealityKit or Metal port of homes-3d-core.js; ShaktiCard data; RingWorld
notes: Design prototype only (JS). Ruling 3: Axis = chakra 18. Ruling 15: Climb's 102 lights stay alike.

title: Rite of entering = the travel (three self-paced beats, three surges of flight)
what: Three self-paced beats (her phrase · her Devanāgarī written by an unseen hand · her roots parting and rejoining over her quality) carry you in three surges of flight until her world's fog swallows everything and the point becomes her room. 'The rite is the distance.' 'Self-paced by touch — never a timer, never skipped, compressed on return.'
how: Each tap advances one beat and one stretch of flight toward her; fog of her world closes; the point becomes the room. On return the beats are compressed via HomeMemory.compression.
needs: ShaktiCard.phrase, dev, roots, quality; stroke-order Devanāgarī rendering; HomeView.swift
notes: Brief: 'Three beats, a few seconds, never skipped, never lingered on.'

title: Room clock: first adaptation 62 s, hold to 227 s, second adaptation reverses premise over 120 s
what: Each room is a mechanism (not a palette) that runs on real elapsed seconds — a first adaptation over 62 s, a hold to 227 s (a 165 s hold), and a second adaptation that reverses the room's premise over 120 s, reachable in practice only through accumulated dwell. RoomState.adaptation 0→1 over 62s; RoomState.second 0→1 over 120s after a 165s hold. 'Every room reverses its premise at the second adaptation. Not more of the same — a reversal.'
how: RoomMechanism.state(at t) → RoomState{adaptation, second, transforms}; label(at t) gives near words and words past second adaptation.
needs: Rooms/RoomMechanism.swift protocol; elapsed-time clock per room
notes: 227 − 62 = 165. 'stay' control runs her clock 14× in prototype.

title: Held attribute as the room's one actor
what: Her Iconography line becomes the room's one actor: a shape performing the single action it exists to perform. Aniconic — a noose is a shape, not a figure. 26 forms; 52 named across the 102. Past the second adaptation the attribute stops being an object — grows into the room (0.9 → 3.16) and thins.
how: ATTRIBUTE map pos→key (52 distinct keys) → one of 26 built forms; ATTR_TINT tints the actor; scale grows with second adaptation.
needs: Rooms/Attribute.swift; ATTRIBUTE + ATTR_TINT from homes-cards.js; 26 form geometries
notes: Code reaches 0.9+2.6=3.5 at full second adaptation vs doc 3.16 — discrepancy. Floor: no figure of a Śakti (aniconic).

title: Doors walk the khaḍgamālā corridor without a cut
what: Khaḍgamālā order is a circle: two named doors per room. A door opens sideways within her neighbourhood first — Ring 2 by cluster, Ring 1 by family — then around the circle. Walking one releases her room and begins the crossing from where you stand, so the rite runs again and there is no cut. 'The homes are one building.'
how: Each room shows two named doors (prev/next neighbour by neighbourhood then circle); walking a door releases current room and runs the rite toward the neighbour from the current point.
needs: R1_FAMILY, R2_CLUSTER, khadgamalaPosition ordering; HomeView doors

title: 'Go deeper' — the descent through five stations of her card
what: Five stations, each ONE field of her card as motion, continuing inward from her room — not a sheet of facts. Her tattva → her location → her etymology → her quality → her phrase. Self-paced.
how: DescentView: five self-paced stations each animating one card field; continues the travel inward.

title: Uniqueness grammar: card field → room role
what: Quality → room's soul ('If a design choice doesn't serve this word, it's wrong for her'). Function → what the room does to you (Aṇimā admits you through a door that should be too small; Mahimā has no far wall). Somatic → physics ('Awareness that becomes smaller than thought' — room contracts; 'Sudden buoyancy' — floor lifts). Bodily Location → body-space & gravity (feet low heavy; crown open-sky; 'Everywhere skin meets world' — no walls, only surface). Iconography → figure/attribute/colour (Mudrā seals are hand-gestures made into rooms). Esoteric Tattva → modifies ring's dhātu ('fire-tattva Śakti in the sapphire/blood ring is warm light inside cool water'). Bīja → tuning: pulse rate, particle rhythm, light-breath locked to syllable. Etymology → threshold ritual. Appreciation Phrase → inscription over her door. Devanagari → what the unseen hand writes. Cluster Group (ring 2) → shared corridor. Shakti Family → lineage register (Siddhis powers, Mātṛkās Mothers with mounts and weapons, Mudrās living hand-seals, Karṣiṇīs pull, Anaṅgas bodiless, Sampradāya cosmic scale, Kulottīrṇa gives, Nigarbha reveals, Vāsinīs speak, Weapons strike, Primordial three ring the Bindu).

title: Carrier from her syllable: VARNA index, JUST ratios, ×2 octave
what: VARNA order (49) a ā i ī u ū ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ e ai o au aṃ aḥ · ka…ṅa · ca…ña · ṭa…ṇa · ta…na · pa…ma · ya ra la va śa ṣa sa ha. Compound bīja → first letter's place. carrier = root × JUST[index mod 12] × 2 ('the interval is hers, the register is ours, and a drone must sit low enough to be felt rather than heard'). No syllable → carrier = root ('silence about what we do not know, rather than a plausible number').

title: Mechanism sentences for 8 authored rooms (verbatim)
what: Aṇimā: 'The door is smaller than you. You are admitted anyway — and then it keeps closing, so the longer you stay the smaller you have become. It never reaches you.' Mahimā: 'Her room has no far wall. Every edge you move toward proves to be the near edge of something larger, arriving out of the haze faster than you can cross it.' Vaśitva: 'The room is not lit — it is known. Only what your attention rests on exists; walls, pillars and her seat resolve inside a travelling pool and fall back to nothing behind it.' Mahātripurasundarī: 'No room at all. The enclosure is gone, and the yantra you have been walking through the whole time stands revealed as the thing you are inside.' Laghimā: 'The floor has released. Her walls end before they reach the ground and their hems lift though there is no wind — everything loose is already on its way up. Nothing in this room falls.' Garimā: 'Her ceiling lowers the entire time you are in it, casting its own weight as shadow, while the floor thickens into strata beneath you. Leaving costs effort no other room asks for.' Sarva-Yoni: 'There is no entrance. The ceremony finds you already within, because no position exists from which you could have arrived. The walls are membrane rather than stone — lit from behind, veined, moving with your breath.' Sarva-Trikhaṇḍā: 'Three rooms occupy the same place, mis-registered like a triple exposure. Move and they part into three. Hold still and they slide into register — one white room, and it was always one room.'
notes: Design's lines count as authored (settled).

title: The method §0–§11 (Design's working rules)
what: §0 'Read everything before making anything … Nothing about the brief caused that. Not reading did.' (all-shaktis-data.js authoritative). §1 'Mechanism, never mood … When a direction arrives as an adjective, convert it to a mechanism out loud and get that confirmed before building.' (Turrell). §2 'Never show the first attempt … push to V2 silently, push to V3 silently'. §3 'Say the plan in plain words, and distrust your own vocabulary … The brief was more radical than the build.' §4 'Fix the rule, not the instance'. §5 'No cuts, only travel … if the user has to choose from a list, the design isn't finished.' §6 'One engine with N tunings, never N artefacts … the mechanism is hers; the light, material and geometry come from her world.' §7 'Build from the real data, degrade gracefully, never invent canon … The gaps are information.' §8 'Verify what the eye can't reach — and verify backwards' (bump ?v=; Object3D.position read-only; clamp gl_PointSize). §9 'Time is elapsed, never device-tied … a high-water mark, not a live reading'. §10 'Never measure it out loud … Depth is felt — a ceremony that runs quicker, a room that opens further along, a light already lit when you arrive.' §11 'Register decisions where they survive the conversation … Anything that lives only in a message is already lost.' Shape: Read → Convert → Concept three passes → Judge → Build engine → Verify by probe → Write decisions. 'Ask when the answer changes what gets built and cannot be derived from the files.'

title: Codex opening: 'This is not an app. It is a temple compressed into glass … The interface is the practice.'
what: Eyebrow 'Codex · Phase I of VIII'; h1 'The Living Yantra'; 'An instrument for recognizing the Mother / through the 102 forces of the Sri Yantra'. 'This is not an app. It is a temple compressed into glass — a living yantra you carry, breathe with, return to. Every interaction is a moment of recognition: of her, in her many forms, present in the texture of your day. The interface is not a wrapper around the practice. The interface is the practice.' 'Five dimensions. Eight modes. No menu. Nine ring-worlds, each with its own atmosphere. The home as a living state, not a screen. A phased path…' 'Read it slowly. Then we begin.' Opening 320×320 yantra with breathing triangle pairs b1/b2/b3.

title: Five dimensions: Depth, Time, Memory, Relationship, Practice
what: Depth (the inward axis) 'Nine avaraṇas as nine depths of consciousness. You move inward, not sideways. Each ring is its own world. You can rest at any depth.' Time (cyclical) 'The yantra breathes with cosmic time. Different shaktis ascend at different hours, moons, seasons. Dawn-yantra is not dusk-yantra.' Memory (accumulation) 'Every recognition leaves a luminous trace. Over months and years, the yantra becomes uniquely yours — bright where you have met her, mystery where you haven't.' Relationship (radial) 'Shaktis cluster around the people in your life. Ram is Ātmā's frequency. Ashrey is Nāma. Gaia is Ahaṅkāra. The work of recognition is inseparable from the work of love.' Practice (modal) 'Eight modes of engagement — not screens, but practices.'
notes: Relationship anchors match ruling 11.

title: Codex eight modes (Devanāgarī, duration, gesture, words)
what: दर्शन Darśana 1–10 min hold vertical 'To be with the yantra without doing anything. The breath finds it. The eye softens. The mind comes home.' · प्रत्यभिज्ञा Recognition ~5 s long-press 'A shakti has just arrived in life. You name her, you receive her, she receives you. The net deployed and retrieved.' · साधना Sādhana 20–30 min pinch 'The Khaḍgamāla — sword-garland — sequential walking through all 102 names with their bījas.' · स्मृति Smṛti long-press ring 'The constellation of past recognitions… The yantra remembers.' · मौन Mauna tap bindu 'The undifferentiated point. All of her, here, always. The place no name reaches. Rest.' · स्वप्न Svapna 3 min morning 'What arrived in the night? Which shakti walked through the dream?' · पूजा Pūjā 5 min evening 'the catches of the day witnessed together. A small offering. The day given back.' · सङ्घ Saṅgha ambient 'Awareness — anonymous, soft — of other practitioners walking the same yantra.' Closing 'The mode is read from the moment. The moment determines the mode. There is no menu to choose from — only the gesture that fits.'

title: Nine-gesture grammar G1–G9 (descend, silence, remember, recite, behold, today's pull, offer, invoke, catch)
what: 'There is no menu.' 'The yantra is the navigation. Every move is a movement of attention — inward, outward, around. Nine gestures form the entire grammar.' G1 Tap a ring descend 'Enter that avaraṇa's world. The ring expands; the others fall away.' G2 Tap the bindu silence 'Mauna. The undifferentiated point. All names gone.' G3 Long-press a ring remember 'Smṛti…' G4 Pinch outward recite 'Sādhana. The Khaḍgamāla begins. All 102 names, sequential.' G5 Hold vertical, still behold 'Darśana. The phone becomes a window.' G6 Swipe up from edge today's pull 'Today's shakti rises. Her name, her bīja, her somatic prompt.' G7 Swipe down from top offer 'Pūjā. Evening only.' G8 Two-finger hold invoke 'Bring a specific shakti into live presence. Bīja-tone plays. She is here.' G9 Long-press anywhere catch 'Freeze the moment. Recognition.' Icons given.
notes: Ruling 10: 'no menu' restriction lifted — gestures remain alongside menu.

what: 'Each avaraṇa is not a sub-page. It is its own world — with its own geometry, light, breath rate, sound, and gravity. A practitioner who has entered Ring 4 knows it by feel.'

what: Trailokyamohana, She Who Enchants the Three Worlds — the ancient ground; warm amber still; square with T-gates; none; 28; glyph #CF9443. 'The world you have already walked through. Earth, surface, the territory of ordinary life. The Bhūpura does not breathe — the ground underfoot is held, not moving. Entering Ring 1 is entering the recognition that the everyday has always been her.'

title: Codex Ring 2 Home lotus: petals bloom in slow wave by cluster colour; wide, generous

'Petals bloom in a slow wave, each cluster a different color — inner instrument, sense streams, citta, stability, self. Tapping a petal opens her detail. The home ring is wide, generous, with room between everything.'

what: Bodiless desires; translucent smoke-like; 8 wide petals; 8s pulse. 'Bodiless longing — the felt-before-it-is-known. Petals appear translucent, edges soft, like smoke catching light. … You feel her without quite seeing her. Tapping a petal: she names herself in italics and dissolves back into the field.'

what: Sovereign grace; rose-violet #C99AB4; 10 inner triangles; 13s deep. 'The field of unasked-for grace. The visual is the most introspective of the rings — narrow, deep, the geometry feels held. Recognition here is the recognition of what protected you when nothing should have worked.'

what: Sound that heals; resonant gold #C9C29A + dashed circles r50/62; 8 triangles + tone rings; 15s with tone pulse. 'The world where language and life have not yet separated. The screen actually resonates — subtle haptic on every breath, a barely-audible bīja tone. Tapping a Vāk-devatā plays her syllable in long, slow attack. This world is a sound chamber as much as a visual one.'
how: Core Haptics pulse on each breath cycle of Ring 7 world.

title: Codex Ring 8: three points; tapping a vertex collapses the other two — 'The visual minimalism is the teaching.'
what: Pure cream against black; three points; 18s almost still; Icchā (top), Kriyā (right), Jñāna (left). 'The entire world is three points. The simplicity is staggering. No ornament. … Tapping any vertex collapses the other two into it — recognition that they were never three. The visual minimalism is the teaching.'

title: Codex Ring 9 Bindu: 'There is nothing else. The whole screen is the point … realizing you have not left.'
what: Sarvanandamaya, She Who Is Made of All Bliss — the undivided; everything & nothing; a single point; your own breath; 1 — Lalitā; crimson 40px orb + 14px cream core glow 30px 8px rgba(139,26,42,.5). 'There is nothing else. The whole screen is the point. This is not a destination — it is what the practice is made of. Every other ring is breathing outward from here. Entering Ring 9 is not arriving; it is realizing you have not left.'

title: Codex §I The Reframe: 'The yantra is the ontology' — not flat; centered; alive
what: 'A content app has tabs because its world is flat — items arranged in categories, each a peer to the next. A consciousness instrument cannot be flat. The structure of awareness is not peer; it is centered. Everything radiates from a center. So this app radiates from the yantra.' 'The Sri Yantra is not a feature inside the app. It is the world the app lives inside. It has presence, mood, time, depth, memory, and relationship. It is not the same yantra at dawn and dusk. It is not the same yantra after a hundred recognitions and zero. It is alive.' 'The architecture is the set of dimensions through which you relate to the yantra. There are five of them.'
notes: Foundation: Home is the Bindu, the centre.

Status is luminosity…' 3 The yantra goes quiet — 'Only the Bindu and the Ring 2 petals keep a breath of life — your two intuitive affordances. The Legend carries all navigation.' 'Four placements … not mutually exclusive … Mix freely.'
